area: Supply chain: static analysis (SAST) of the app's Python and JavaScript, offline in every test run (bandit) and in CI (CodeQL)
title: Wave 7: bandit 1.9.4 added to the dev lock and gating every test run at medium severity and up; CodeQL security-extended for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript on pull requests and weekly; every current bandit finding triaged
baseline: origin/dev 1b2420b: no static analyser anywhere (sbd-auth check scorecard-sast open)

checks.what: bandit over every Python file outside tests/ (128 files, 89,741 lines) with every check enabled, no skips: no finding of medium severity or higher at any confidence after the triage below
Every # nosec names its check and gives a reason after a second #, is on tests/test_sast.py's reviewed list (7) and still silences a live finding; no bare # nosec
The gate fails on a planted shell=True, yaml.load, md5, ElementTree.fromstring or os.system in app code, and ignores the same code under tests/

bandit and its dependencies (stevedore; PyYAML, rich, markdown-it-py, mdurl at requirements.lock's pins) hash-pinned in requirements-dev.lock, compiled with the Makefile's lock-dev command against requirements.lock without --upgrade (no other pin moved); pyproject's dev extra pins bandit==1.9.4

CodeQL workflow: pull requests to dev, qa and main that change code, weekly (Monday 04:37 UTC) and on demand; python and javascript-typescript, security-extended; one ubuntu-latest job, 20-minute limit, concurrency cancels a stale run; contents: read at the top, security-events: write (and actions: read) only on the analysis job; checkout and codeql-action pinned by full commit SHA (codeql-action v4.39.1 = 9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370, read from the official repository's tag with git ls-remote)
checks.standard: Scorecard SAST · Scorecard Token-Permissions · Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies

checks.what: CodeQL's first run: not yet run, GitHub Actions minutes are exhausted on this account; on a private repository code scanning also needs GitHub Advanced Security (Code Security) enabled, or the upload step fails

Low B110/B112 (100): try/except pass or continue. Best-effort cleanup (closing a classic session, removing a temp file), optional module loads and display fallbacks; none hides a security decision (the write gates, scope and token checks raise or refuse, they do not pass). Not gated; left as is

Low B105/B107 (51): 'hardcoded password' on status words (PASS/FAIL), labels, header and cookie names, environment-variable names, empty ZCC password fields in a disabled template, the offline tenant's fixed marker and the Terraform assessor placeholder. Each read: no credential in the code

Low B404/B603/B607 (54): subprocess with an argument list, never a shell; programs are git, the running Python, terraform, powershell with a fixed script, taskkill; the branch passed to git ls-remote is validated against the allowed list first. Not gated
Low B101 (22): assert in tools/verify_native_install.py, a CI verification script whose asserts are its checks (never run with -O); none in the app
Low B311 (2): random.Random(seed) in tools/validate_detection.py builds a reproducible synthetic test corpus, not a secret; the app's tokens use secrets
Low B405/B406 (3): imports of xml.etree (both parse sites refuse DOCTYPE and ENTITY first, see W7-SAST-03) and xml.sax.saxutils.escape (an escaper, parses nothing)

findings.title: SHA-1 used for ids without usedforsecurity=False (guidance._slug, pack_library.pack_slug): not a security use, but a FIPS-mode OpenSSL refuses a plain sha1(), so those ids would fail there (bandit B324, high/high)
findings.fix: Both pass usedforsecurity=False; the ids are unchanged

findings.title: B104 (bind to all interfaces, medium) on 0.0.0.0 compared to word the start-up address and a notice (dlp_api_server.main), as an address-family probe (workload_path._is_address) and in the standalone smoke test's hostile environment and address compare: nothing binds
findings.reason: False positive: each literal moved to one named constant with # nosec B104 and its reason (3 suppressions for 5 hits); the real bind checks are security.py's and are tested

findings.title: B314 (ElementTree.fromstring on untrusted XML, medium) in vendor_migrate (2) and tools/quality_score.run_from_junit
findings.reason: False positive: each parse runs only after _refuse_dtd refused any DOCTYPE or ENTITY in any encoding, on input size-capped first; # nosec B314 with that reason on each

findings.title: B202 (tarfile.extractall without validation, high) on tools/smoke_standalone.unpack's zipfile.extractall; B310 (urlopen scheme, medium) on its http://127.0.0.1 requests
findings.reason: False positives in a developer tool: bandit sees tarfile imported (the tar branch already uses filter=data); zipfile strips absolute and .. paths and makes no links; the URLs are the tool's own loopback ones

findings.title: B608 (SQL built from strings, medium/low) on app_update's error message: 'update stopped ... set aside' matched bandit's UPDATE ... SET pattern
findings.reason: False positive (the app has no SQL): the message now says put aside, so no suppression is needed

notes: make sast and tests/test_sast.py run the same command: python -m bandit -c pyproject.toml -r . --severity-level medium --confidence-level low. bandit's exclude_dirs match as substrings of ./path, so the target must be . from the repository root.
The suppression form is # nosec <id> # <why>: with # nosec <id>: <why> bandit reads every word of the reason as a check name and logs a warning for each.
A whole-repository scan takes about 17 seconds; the stale-suppression check rescans only the five files that hold one.
CodeQL is path-filtered on pull requests (code and the workflow only). If it is ever made a required check, drop the paths filter or a docs-only pull request will wait for it.
